about: The Actus contritionis is an individual penitential prayer. It expresses repentance for and detestation of every sin, acknowledges just punishment, and makes the offense against God, the supreme Good worthy of love above all things, the foremost motive of contrition. It ends with a firm resolve, helped by grace, to sin no more and to avoid near occasions of sin.

seg.tr: My God, I am sorry with my whole heart for all my sins,

ex.w012: The speaker does not merely repent but rejects and detests the sins.

seg.tr: not only because in sinning I have deserved the punishments You have justly decreed,
but especially because I have offended You, who are the highest good and worthy of love above all things.
Therefore, aided by Your grace, I firmly resolve never to sin again

ex.w040: The phrase “grátia tua adiuvánte” ascribes future fidelity to the help of God’s grace.
ex.w044: The fixed phrase “de cétero” marks a prospective boundary: henceforth, from now on.

seg.tr: and to shun the near occasions of sin. Amen.

ex.w050: A moral term denoting near occasions, not every remote circumstance in which sin is possible.
